thread:
maria: Heads-up - restore job for tenant-42 failing with KMS DecryptAccessDenied for some snapshots (errors cluster at 2026-02-14 backups).
jen-security: Can you paste the error from the restore logs?
tom-backup: sample error: 
```\nException: DecryptAccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::0123456789:assumed-role/restore-runner is not authorized to use key arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:0123456789:key/old-cmk-id\n```
maria: This started after yesterday's RBAC cleanup where we pruned some cross-account grants for old service roles. Might have been too aggressive.
raj-iam: I see a policy prune job ran at 03:12Z and removed grants labelled `legacy-upload-grant`. It looks like that grant was still in use by uploader->kms for snapshots created in 2025.
jen-security: Immediate mitigation: re-grant Decrypt on the CMK to the `restore-runner` principal for the affected key IDs. Can we script a scoped grant so it's temporary?
raj-iam: yes. I'll create an ephemeral KMS grant valid for 24h scoped to the exact key ARNs and the restore-runner principal. Command:
```\naws kms create-grant --key-id <key-id> --grantee-principal arn:aws:iam::0123456789:role/restore-runner --operations Decrypt\n```
I'll add GrantTokens to the restore process.
tom-backup: adding GrantTokens fixes the restore in my local re-run for one sample snapshot. Restarts look good.
maria: post-mitigation: we need a retro to decide which grants are safe to prune. Also inventory keys with legacy grants and map to snapshot creation ranges.
jen-security: follow-ups: 1) add a check to the RBAC-prune job to skip KMS grants with active references in backups metadata, 2) alert when grants are removed for CMKs in the `redwood-backups` key alias, 3) document a restore playbook for ephemeral re-grants.
security-bot: Incident created INC-2026-251 (severity=P2) - responders: @maria @jen-security @tom-backup @raj-iam
maria: I'll own the postmortem and compile the snapshot->key mapping. Raj, paste the grant create commands and TTLs into the incident doc. Tom, continue validation of restored snapshots.
